title: Things, places and big ideas
theme: everyday nouns, abstract nouns and small linking words
goal: Recognise and use 25 high-frequency nouns and adverbs for everyday things, health, places and abstract ideas.

example.fr: C'est quoi, ce truc ?
example.en: What's this thing?

items.note: **Informal.** Very common when you can't find the word. In Québec you also hear *une patente*.

example.fr: En hiver, j'ai la peau très sèche.
example.en: In winter, my skin is very dry.

example.fr: Je me suis coupé le doigt en cuisinant.
example.en: I cut my finger while cooking.

items.note: The g and t are silent: [dwa]. A toe is *un orteil*.

example.fr: Ce soir, la lune est pleine.
example.en: Tonight the moon is full.

example.fr: Ma fille fait du cheval le samedi.
example.en: My daughter goes horseback riding on Saturdays.

example.fr: Mets les sacs dans le coffre.
example.en: Put the bags in the trunk.

items.note: In Québec, the car trunk is usually *la valise (de l'auto)*. *Un coffre-fort* is a safe.

example.fr: Le chien court après la balle.
example.en: The dog is running after the ball.

items.note: A big ball (soccer, basketball) is *un ballon*.

example.fr: Elle est à la fac depuis deux ans.
example.en: She's been at university for two years.

items.note: **Informal** (France). Short for *la faculté*. In Québec, people say *l'université*; before that, many students go to the *cégep*.

example.fr: Les résultats du labo arrivent demain.
example.en: The lab results come tomorrow.

example.fr: Il a passé deux ans en prison.
example.en: He spent two years in prison.

example.fr: La drogue est un problème dans ce quartier.
example.en: Drugs are a problem in this neighbourhood.

items.note: False friend: medicine from the pharmacy is *un médicament*, never *une drogue*.

example.fr: Sa mère a guéri d'un cancer.
example.en: Her mother recovered from cancer.

example.fr: Le peuple a voté pour le changement.
example.en: The people voted for change.

items.note: For “people” in general, use *les gens*: *Les gens sont gentils ici.*

example.fr: Laisse-moi en paix, je travaille.
example.en: Leave me in peace, I'm working.

example.fr: Pitié, pas encore la neige !
example.en: Oh please, not snow again!

items.note: *Avoir pitié de quelqu'un* = to feel sorry for someone.

example.fr: C'est le destin : on s'est rencontrés à Vancouver.
example.en: It's fate: we met in Vancouver.

items.en: universe; world (of a person or field)

example.fr: J'adore l'univers de ce réalisateur.
example.en: I love this director's world.

example.fr: Partir en voiture par cette tempête ? C'est de la folie !
example.en: Driving off in this storm? It's madness!

example.fr: La beauté de la Gaspésie m'a impressionnée.
example.en: The beauty of the Gaspé Peninsula impressed me.

example.fr: Il a enfin trouvé son âme sœur.
example.en: He has finally found his soulmate.

example.fr: Tu sais garder un secret ?
example.en: Can you keep a secret?

example.fr: Il y a des traces de pas dans la neige.
example.en: There are footprints in the snow.

example.fr: Apparemment, le bureau est fermé lundi.
example.en: Apparently, the office is closed on Monday.

example.fr: Il a neigé durant toute la nuit.
example.en: It snowed throughout the night.

items.note: Means the same as *pendant*, which is more common in speech.

example.fr: Les enfants dorment là-haut.
example.en: The kids are sleeping upstairs.

items.note: The opposite is *en bas* (down there, downstairs). Don't confuse it with *là-bas* (over there).

blocks.title: False friends and Québec
blocks.body: [[Une drogue]] is an illegal drug; medicine is [[un médicament]]. [[Le peuple]] is a nation; everyday “people” is [[les gens]]. A small ball is [[une balle]], a big one [[un ballon]]. In Québec, the car trunk is often [[la valise]], and students go to [[l'université]] or the [[cégep]] rather than *la fac*.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.tip: The c of truc is pronounced.

lines.fr: En hiver, j'ai la peau très sèche.
lines.en: In winter, my skin is very dry.

lines.fr: Je me suis coupé le doigt en cuisinant.
lines.en: I cut my finger while cooking.

lines.fr: Mets les sacs dans le coffre.
lines.en: Put the bags in the trunk.

lines.fr: Les résultats du labo arrivent demain.

lines.en: Leave me in peace, I'm working.

lines.fr: Apparemment, le bureau est fermé lundi.
lines.en: Apparently, the office is closed on Monday.

lines.fr: Il y a des traces de pas dans la neige.
lines.en: There are footprints in the snow.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. Getting something wrong now helps you remember it later.

blocks.prompt: Amira has a headache and goes to the pharmacy. What does she buy?
blocks.explain: Medicine is [[un médicament]]. [[Une drogue]] is an illegal drug.
optionFeedback: False friend: une drogue is an illegal drug.
une balle is a small ball.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means “People are friendly here”?
blocks.explain: For people in general, use [[les gens]]. [[Le peuple]] means a nation or the people as a political group.
optionFeedback: le peuple = a nation, the people as a whole (politics).

blocks.prompt: Apparently, the lab is closed today.
accept: Apparemment, le labo est fermé aujourd'hui.
Apparemment, le laboratoire est fermé aujourd'hui.
Apparemment le labo est fermé aujourd'hui.
Apparemment le laboratoire est fermé aujourd'hui.
Le labo est fermé aujourd'hui, apparemment.
Le laboratoire est fermé aujourd'hui, apparemment.
blocks.explain: [[Apparemment]] usually starts the sentence, followed by a comma.

blocks.prompt: Put the bags in the trunk. (to a friend)
accept: Mets les sacs dans le coffre.
Mets les sacs dans la valise.
Mets les sacs dans le coffre de la voiture.
Mets les sacs dans la valise de l'auto.
Mets les sacs dans le coffre de l'auto.
Mets les sacs dans la valise de la voiture.
blocks.explain: The trunk of a car is [[le coffre]]; in Québec you will often hear [[la valise]].
[[Garder un secret]] = to keep a secret.

blocks.text: Il a neigé ___ toute la nuit.

blocks.explain: [[là-haut]]: là has a grave accent, and there is a hyphen.

blocks.fr: Partir en voiture par cette tempête ? C'est de la folie !
blocks.en: Driving off in this storm? It's madness!

summary:
- Name everyday things: [[le truc, la peau, le doigt, la lune, le cheval, le coffre, la balle]]
- Talk about places and health: [[la fac, le labo, la prison, la drogue, le cancer]]
- Use abstract nouns: [[la paix, le destin, la folie, la beauté, l'âme, le secret]]
- Avoid false friends: [[une drogue]] ≠ medicine, [[le peuple]] ≠ people in general
